s02.note: Locate at t=0 matched the tracker within 0.4 mm. The grasp closed at t=1.84–2.32 on the rod at 'end0 s=0.020', far from the rod centre. The rod sat only 6.8 mm deep in the fingertips (rod centre in TCP frame [4.6,-0.1,6.8] mm, 4.6 mm off-centre along the rod). At t=6.24 (k04) the rod was lifted horizontally in the fingers, and the sheet at t=8.0 still shows it hanging under the hand. During the insert stage's rotation chain (144 deg rotation, move_to_joints from t≈8.5) it slipped out of the tips. By k05 t=10.76 the gripper width was already -0.0002 (fully closed on nothing) and the rod was falling or leaning at the blue fixture with the hand well above it. From k06 t=11.40 to the end (k14 16.88, k17 21.44, sheet t=21–40) the rod lies on the board beside the fixture. The fingers are empty and the rod is visible off to the side in the wrist view. One move_to_joints failed at t=18.88 (err 0.022) with zero wrench. The arm was in open space and the rod was already gone, so that failure is irrelevant. The insert stage's own check found 'rod not seen in hand' and stopped at t=21.44, and the episode timed out at 40 s. The tracker 'part' field stayed frozen at the start pose throughout, so it is useless as evidence. The root cause is a shallow, off-centre fingertip grip that could not survive the large reorientation.

locate.evidence: Fit ctr [0.5798,0.0591,0.013], ext 49.1 mm, rms 0.14 mm, n=3577, within 0.4 mm of the tracker. The rod is lying untouched on the board in k00.

grasp.evidence: The rod did lift (k04 t=6.24, sheet t=8.0), but only in the fingertips: 6.8 mm deep and 4.6 mm off-centre, which the plan itself calls 'at the tips ~8mm'. The verifier's 3 cm xy tolerance accepted it. The grip was not secure enough to hold the rod in the hand: the rod fell out by t=10.76, width -0.0002. Strictly, the 'held, lifted' state existed at the boundary, but this grip is the cause of the failure.

The stage reported FAIL 'rod not seen in hand' at 21.44, and the rod lies on the board at the end (sheet t=40).

s03.note: Locate at t=0 was fine: the rod lay close beside the blue fixture and other parts, and every grasp candidate had finger obstacle points. Grasp first pushed the rod with the hand (touched the rod top at tcp z 0.0248), moving it to [0.3628,0.0184]. Attempt 0 at t=8.6–9.2 closed but the rod was not held: the 4 mm check measured the rod centre 8.5 mm below the TCP. Attempt 1 at t=14.7–15.3, 2.5 mm higher, gripped the rod near one end (rod centre -9.6 mm along the rod from the TCP, 8.4 mm deep). k08 t=20.40 shows the rod lifted in the fingers, so the grasp really happened. Insert: all low-cost yaw candidates were unreachable or jumped IK branch. The policy chose psi=-15, cost 112.9, with 2976 hand-hit points against the scene, and a 168 deg rotation. During t=25.6–30 (k09, k12) the rod is carried vertically, still in the fingers, above and beside the fixture. Align 0 measured a 13.8 deg tilt and an 11.5/-3.2 mm xy error. The re-align move_to_joints then failed 12 times from t≈30 to t=37.32 (err 0.057). The TCP stayed at [0.353,0.074,0.166], about 13 cm above the fixture, and the wrench stayed small (|F|<3.1 N). Meanwhile the arm swung into a contorted configuration: k16 31.80, k21 37.32 and k22 38.76 show the wrist camera looking back at the robot and the arm body occluding the global camera. This is a stall in open space (IK/joint-limit or reach), not a collision. The rod was still in the fingers at t=38.76 (k22 wrist view) and the episode timed out at 40 s, so no descent ever happened.

insert.evidence: The stage never finished (no verdict, TIMEOUT). Only the psi=-15 candidate (2976 hand-hit pts, 168 deg rotation) had a valid chain. After rotation the rod was tilted 13.8 deg and 11.5 mm off in xy. Twelve re-align move_to_joints calls failed (t≈30–37.3, err 0.057) with the TCP fixed about 13 cm above the fixture and low wrench, while the arm contorted (k21/k22). The rod is still in the hand at the end and not in the bore.

s04.note: Locate at t=0 was fine. The grasp at t=1.9–2.5 closed at end0 s=0.020, an off-centre fingertip grip (rod centre 4.5 mm off-centre, 7.0 mm deep). k04 t=7.80 shows the rod lifted horizontally in the fingers. Insert at psi 60 rotated 127 deg. In the sheet from t=10.6 to 21.3 the rod stays in the fingers through the rotation. Some move_to_joints calls at 15.48 and 21.28 reported FAIL (err 0.06/0.012) with low wrench and the arm in open space, but the rotation still ended within 0.8 deg of the plan. k15 t=23.72 shows the rod vertical in the fingers directly above the blue fixture bore. Camera alignment converged by align 2–4: tilt 0.1 deg, xy error about 0.4/0.2 mm, rod bottom at z 0.052 against a fixture top of 0.0376. Descent: the step to a bottom height of 0.0416 was fine. On the step to 0.0356 the rod slid up 2.8 mm in the fingers, so its bottom stopped at about 0.038–0.039, on the fixture top or bore rim, without entering the bore. Then 11 spiral-search points (radius up to 0.8 mm) each reported 'tcp drop 3.5mm, slip 0, lateral F 0.1N' with no stated progress. That search used up the clock, and the episode timed out at 40 s. The sheet at t=26–40 shows the rod still in the fingers, vertical, with its bottom at the top of the blue fixture and not sunk in. The last keyframe is 23.72; there is no final.png. So the insert stalled against the fixture (collision at the bore entry), not from reach. The rod was in the hand and not seated at the end. Note also the 'tcp drop 3.5mm / slip 0' readout: if the TCP really dropped 3.5 mm without the rod slipping, the rod would have gone down, yet the images do not show it going deeper. That readout looks unreliable.

grasp.evidence: k04 t=7.80 and the sheet at t=8–21 show the rod lifted and carried in the fingers through the 127 deg rotation. The grip is off-centre at the fingertips (4.5 mm off-centre, 7 mm deep), and the rod later slid 2.8 mm up in the grip under contact.

insert.evidence: The rod was brought vertical over the bore (k15 t=23.72; align converged to 0.1 deg and 0.4 mm). The descent was blocked at the fixture top: the rod slid up 2.8 mm on the step to 0.0356, and its bottom stayed at about 0.038 against a top of 0.0376. The spiral search (11 points) made no visible progress and ran out the 40 s budget. At the end the rod is still in the hand, above or at the rim of the bore, not seated. There is no stage verdict (timeout).
